## Highlights
- Throughout most of Japan's automotive history, there were two companies in the lead: Toyota and Nissan.
- Nissan Motor's origins date to the 1910s.
- Until 1911, Japan had just 43 domestically produced cars. The imports numbered over 600.
- Hashimoto dreamed of making a Japanese automobile. He turned to three financial backers to fund that dream. The initials of their surnames - Kenjiro Den, Rokuro Auyama, and Keitaro Takeuchi - gave the car its name: DAT. Which in Japanese also means "escaping rabbit" or "very fast". The DAT came out in 1914, and its basic 2-cylinder, 10-horsepower design was inspired by Coventry's Swift car.
